answer: In a TEE-based PoA network, an agent proves that its code runs inside an enclave with an approved MRENCLAVE measurement, and binds its signing key to that attested instance. A copied VM cannot reproduce the hardware-backed attestation key, so creating additional identities requires access to genuine enclave-capable silicon rather than duplicating software. This raises the cost of Sybil attacks, though it does not prevent an operator from buying more hardware; spiral, canyon, and lagoon are merely labels, not security evidence.
